newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Commodities and manufactureds lead Brazil exports.
newsitem.headline: Commodities and manufactureds lead Brazil exports.

text.p: Brazilian exports of manufactured and primary goods hit record levels in 1996 but lower global commodities prices and a recovery in domestic demand put a brake on export growth last year, a senior trade official said.

Mauricio Cortes, secretary of foreign trade at the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, said overseas sales of primary products rose 11.08 percent in 1996 from 1995 to reach $12.184 billion, or 25.52 percent of all exports.
Manufactured goods posted sales of $26.393 billion, up 3.24 percent on 1995.
But Cortes said semimanufactured goods, which made up 17.49 percent of all 1996 exports, slumped 8.67 percent over 1995 to $8.353 billion.
Overall, 1996 exports of $47.746 billion were 2.67 percent higher than in 1995.

"The 1996 exports showed a lower increase (over 1995) compared with 1994-95, when exports rose 6.8 percent. This largely reflects the circumstances dominating international trade and internal factors," Cortes said, reading a statement.
Cortes noted that commodities prices in 1996 were broadly down and said the main goods affected were paper, coffee, semimanufactured iron and steel products, aluminium and copper.
The Ministry of Industry and Commerce estimated that revenue loss from lower world prices amounted to some $1.9 billion.

Cortes said that Brazil's policy of gradual monetary flexibilization in 1996, which resulted in a surge in economic activity in the second half, had also persuaded manufacturers to sell to the hungry domestic market instead of overseas.

December's $3.789 billion exports, within expectations but nevertheless on the low side, reinforced predictions of a massive trade gap that month of up to $1.5 billion, which would be a monthly record.
Such a result would take the 1996 trade gap to about $5.2 billion, a significant rise on 1995's $3.157 billion deficit.
December exports were in line with forecasts from eight banks and research firms surveyed by Reuters. The consensus forecast from the survey put exports at $3.83 billion in December.
